Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:12:1.hebrew: כדרבי חנינא - בפ' קמא (לעיל בכורות ה:): מה נשתנו פטרי חמורים מפטרי סוסים וגמלים כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:12:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Ḥanina - In the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 5b): "In what way are firstborn donkeys different from firstborn horses and camels, etc.?"

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:12:2.hebrew: דזוטרן מיליה - דלא מיירי בפטר חמור אלא פרקא קמא, וכולה מסכתא איירי בבכור בהמה טהורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:12:2.english: Since its matters are few - For it deals with the firstborn of a donkey only [in] the first chapter, and the entire [rest of the] tractate deals with the firstborn of a kosher animal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:13:1.english: For his animal - For his herd.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:13:2.hebrew: בדיניהן - דיינינן ליה בדיניהן, ולקמן מפרש מאי היא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:13:2.english: According to their laws - We judge him according to their laws, and further on [the Gemara] explains what this is.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:16:1.hebrew: אחוזה נקנית בכסף ובשטר ובחזקה - מכי דייש אמיצרי, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כו.):
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:16:1.english: An ancestral possession is acquired by money, or with a deed, or through taking possession - [Taking possession is effective] from [the moment] he treads on the boundaries, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (26a):

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:17:1.hebrew: וממונו במשיכה - מטלטלין אין נקנין אלא במשיכה, במסכת קדושין (דף כו.):
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:17:1.english: And his property by pulling - Movable property is acquired only by pulling, [as stated] in Tractate Kiddushin (26a).

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:18:1.hebrew: מיד עמיתך - משמע מיד ליד, דהיינו משיכה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:18:1.english: From the hand of your counterpart - This implies [transfer] from hand to hand, which is pulling:

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:19:1.hebrew: כלל כלל לא - עד שתבא לרשותו של ישראל, לא קני:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:19:1.english: Not at all - Until it comes into the domain of the Jew, he does not acquire [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:1:1.hebrew: רב ששת אמר - לעולם מצות פדיון לאלתר. והאי דקתני ״אין בערכין ופטר חמור פחות משלשים״ — שאינו עובר עליו עד שלשים יום; מכאן ואילך, עובר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:1:1.english: Rav Sheshet said - Actually, the mitzvah of redemption [applies] immediately. And that which was taught: “There is [nothing] in [the laws of] valuations and firstborn donkeys [in] less than thirty [days]” — [means] that one does not transgress [the command] regarding it until thirty days; from this [point] forward, he transgresses.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:20:1.hebrew: ואימא או בהא או בהא - והכי משמע קרא: "מיד עמיתך" הוא דבמשיכה ולא בכסף, הא מיד עובד כוכבים — באיזה שתרצה. ונשמע מיניה, דהיכא דמשך ולא נתן מעו', נמי קני:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:20:1.english: And say: Either through this or through that - And this is what the verse implies: It is [only] "from the hand of your counterpart" that [an acquisition is] through pulling and not through money, whereas from the hand of a gentile, [it may be] through whichever [method] you wish. And we would derive from it that where he pulled and did not give money, he also acquires.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:21:1.english: Just as your counterpart [is] with one - Pulling.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:21:2.hebrew: אף עובד כוכבים בחדא - בכסף ולא במשיכה, דהכי משמע: עמיתך במשיכה, ולא עובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:21:2.english: So too, a gentile [is] with one [act] - With money, and not with pulling; for this is what [the verse] implies: "Your counterpart" [is acquired] with pulling, but not a gentile.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:22:1.english: From the money of his purchase - The verse is speaking of a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:2:1.hebrew: מאי לאו מצוה להשהותו - כרב נחמן, וקשיא לרב ששת:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:2:1.english: What, [is it] not a mitzva to delay it - In accordance with [the view of] Rav Naḥman, and [this poses] a difficulty for Rav Sheshet.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:2:2.hebrew: מצוה לפדותו - דמלאלתר עד שלשים הוי זמן פדייה, ומכאן ואילך עובר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:2:2.english: A mitzva to redeem it - That from immediately [after birth] until thirty [days] is the time of redemption, and from that point forward he transgresses.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:3:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - לעולם מצוה לשהותו, ואפי' הכי כרב נחמן לא מתריצנא. ולא קשיא: הא דקתני שלשים יום — מצוה לשהותו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:3:1.english: Rather, Rava said - Actually, [there is] a mitzvah to delay it, and even so, we do not resolve [the contradiction] like Rav Naḥman. And [it is] not difficult: that which taught thirty days [holds that it is] a mitzvah to delay it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:3:2.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer who compares - The firstborn of an impure animal to the firstborn of a human.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:3:3.hebrew: והא - דקתני לאלתר, רבנן היא דמתניתין, דלא מקשו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:3:3.english: And that - which teaches “immediately” is [the opinion of] the Rabbis of our Mishnah, who do not compare [them].

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:5:1.hebrew: מצות יעידה - באמה העבריה, שייעדנה אדון לאשה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:5:1.english: The mitzva of designation - [This applies] to a Hebrew maidservant, that the master designate her as a wife.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:5:2.english: Takes precedence over the mitzva of redemption - That she redeems herself.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:5:3.hebrew: אשר לא יעדה והפדה - אם יעדה, זה מוטב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:5:3.english: Who has not designated her, then he shall let her be redeemed - If he designates her, that is preferable.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:6:1.hebrew: עכשיו מצות חליצה קודמת - שהמייבם את יבמתו שלא לשם מצוה, פוגע באיסור אשת אח:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:6:1.english: Now the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence - For one who performs levirate marriage with his yevama not for the sake of the mitzva violates the prohibition of a brother's wife.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:7:1.hebrew: באדון - במתפיס בהמה טמאה לבדק הבית, מצות פדייתה באדון קודם לכל אדם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:7:1.english: By the owner - In [the case of] one who consecrates a non-kosher animal to the Temple maintenance, the mitzvah of its redemption is by the owner, [who] takes precedence over any [other] person.

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:9:1.english: One who purchases the fetus of a cow:

Rashi on Bekhorot 13a:9:2.english: [Even though] one is not permitted - To sell an animal to a gentile.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:13:1.hebrew: קנה וחייבת בבכורה - ואע"ג דשמעינן "קנה", איצטריך לאשמועינן דחייבת בבכורה — דלא תימא קנה מספק או מדרבנן; קמ"ל דקנה קנין גמור:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:13:1.english: "He has acquired [it], and it is obligated in the firstborn" - And even though we learn "he has acquired [it]," it was necessary to teach us that it is obligated in the firstborn — lest you say [that] he acquired [it] out of uncertainty or rabbinically; [therefore,] it teaches us that he acquired [it with] a full acquisition.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:16:1.hebrew: מה אחוזה נקנית בכסף ובשטר ובחזקה - פירוש: כשקונה מישראל; אף עבד כנעני כן, כשקונין מישראל. אבל בעובד כוכבים, לא מסתבר שיועיל שטר, לפי שקנין שטר לא שייך בעובד כוכבים, כדאמרי' פ' חזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נד:): "עובד כוכבים מכי מטא זוזי לידיה איסתליק ליה, וישראל לא קני עד דמטא שטרא לידיה":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:16:1.english: "Just as an ancestral possession is acquired by money, and with a deed, and through taking possession" - Explanation: [This applies] when one purchases from an Israelite; [and] so too, a Canaanite slave is such when they purchase [him] from an Israelite. But regarding a gentile, it is not reasonable that a deed would be effective, because acquisition by a deed does not apply to a gentile, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 54b): "A gentile, once the money reaches his hand, withdraws [his ownership], and an Israelite does not acquire [it] until the deed reaches his hand."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:18:1.hebrew: מיד עמיתך במשיכה הא מיד עובד כוכבים בכסף - וא"ת: דלמא הא מיד עובד כוכבים בשטר ובחזקה, דחזקה נמי שייכא במטלטלין, אם עשה בהן שום תיקון כעין נעל וגדר ופרץ בקרקע? י"ל: דשני קנייני' הללו הויין מצויין, ושייכי זה במוכר וזה בלוקח — שזה נותן מעות וזה מושך אצלו החפץ. וכן לרבי יוחנן בסמוך, דדרשינן איפכא: "מיד עמיתך בכסף, הא לעובד כוכבים במשיכה". וא"ת: מנלן שהן חשובין קנין כלל, דמוקמינן מסברא קנינין דקרא בהני? י"ל: דאשכחן כסף שקונה במקום אחר — בקרקע ובהקדש, ומשיכה — במציאה והפקר:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:18:1.english: “[From] the hand of your counterpart” [is] through pulling, but from the hand of a gentile [is] with money - And if you say: Perhaps “from the hand of a gentile” [is] through a deed or through [an act of] possession, for [an act of] possession also applies to movable property if one made any improvement to them, similar to locking, fencing, or breaching in [the case of] land? One can say: These two [modes of] acquisition are common, and are pertinent, one to the seller and one to the buyer — for this one gives money and that one pulls the item to himself. And likewise according to Rabbi Yochanan nearby, where we expound conversely: “From the hand of your counterpart” [is] with money, but for a gentile [it is] through pulling. And if you say: From where do we know that they are considered an acquisition at all, such that we establish the acquisitions of the verse as these by logical reasoning? One can say: Because we find that money effects acquisition elsewhere — regarding land and regarding consecrated property; and pulling [effects acquisition] regarding a found object and ownerless property.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:22:1.hebrew: (לעיל) אם גופו קני - אם גופו דישראל קני ליה עובד כוכבים בכסף כו', מדלא פריך הכא: "אם כן, אפי' בשטר וחזקה נמי!", כדפריך לעיל — יש ראיה לפר"ת, דמפרש פרק קמא דקדושין (דף יד:): "אשכחן עבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים שכל קניינו בכסף", כלומר: כל קנינו דעובד כוכבים בעבד עברי בכסף, כדכתיב (ויקרא כה): "מכסף מקנתו", ולא בשטר וחזקה, כדמוכח הכא. ובקונטרס פי' שם, דכל דבר קניינו בכסף, כדדרשינן הכא: "מיד עמיתך" — במשיכה, הא מיד עובד כוכבים — בכסף. וקשה, דהאי דרשא לריש לקיש היא, והלכה כר' יוחנן. וא"ת: אכתי עובד כוכבי' קונה ישראל בחזקה, כדאמר גיטין (דף לח.): "מנין לעובד כוכבים שקונה ישראל בחזקה? שנאמר: וישב ממנו שבי"! י"ל: דההיא חזקה — כשיש מלחמה הוא, והוא הדין ממונו, כדאמר חולין (דף ס:): "עמון ומואב טיהרו בסיחון":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:22:1.english: (Above) "If [a gentile] acquires his person" - "If a gentile acquires the person of an Israelite with money, etc." — From [the fact] that [the Gemara] does not object here: "If so, [he should] also [acquire him] through a deed or an act of possession [chazakah]!", as it objected above, there is proof for the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, who explains [the statement in] the first chapter of Kiddushin (14b): "We have found that with regard to a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile, his entire acquisition is with money" — that is to say, all of a gentile's acquisition of a Hebrew slave is with money, as it is written (Leviticus 25:51): "From the money of his purchase," and not through a deed or an act of possession, as is proven here. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained there that any item, its acquisition is with money, as we interpret homiletically here: "[If you sell an acquisition] to the hand of your fellow" — [it is acquired] through pulling, but from the hand of a gentile — [it is acquired] with money. And this is difficult, for this derivation is in accordance with Reish Lakish, whereas the halakha follows Rabbi Yochanan. And if you say: Still, a gentile acquires an Israelite through an act of possession, as [the Gemara] says in Gittin (38a): "From where is it derived that a gentile acquires an Israelite through an act of possession? As it is stated: 'And he took some of them captive'" (Numbers 21:1)? It can be said: That act of possession is when there is war, and the same law applies to his property, as [the Gemara] says in Chullin (60b): "Ammon and Moab became purified through Sihon."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:24:1.hebrew: אימא לעובד כוכבים כלל כלל לא קל וחומר אם גופו קני ממונו לא כל שכן - וא"ת: דלמא בחליפין דהוא מקני ממונו? כדדריש בקדושין (דף ח.): "מכסף מקנתו" — בכסף הוא נקנה, ואינו נקנה בתורת תבואה וכלים; ומאי נינהו? חליפין. ובעבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים כתיב האי קרא, משמע: הא שאר, כגון מטלטלין, קונה עובד כוכבים בחליפין! וי"ל: דאי לא אשכחן כסף או משיכה בעובד כוכבים, לא הוה מוקמינן ליה בחליפין. ועי"ל: האי דקאמר "עובד כוכבים בחדא", לאו בחליפין ששוה בעובד כוכבים ובישראל מיירי, אלא בקנין חדש, כגון כסף או משיכה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:24:1.english: Say: To a gentile, not at all? [Isn't it] an a fortiori inference: If he acquires his person, does he not all the more so [acquire] his property? - And if you say: Perhaps it is through chalifin [symbolic barter] that his property is acquired, as [the Gemara] expounds in Kiddushin (8a): “From the money of his purchase” (Leviticus 25:51) — with money he is acquired, and he is not acquired through the rule of produce and vessels; and what are they? Chalifin. And this verse is written regarding a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile, which implies: but other [items], such as movable property, a gentile acquires through chalifin! And one can say: If we had not found money or pulling [to be effective] for a gentile, we would not establish it through chalifin. And further, one can say: That which [the Gemara] said, “a gentile [acquires] with one [mode of acquisition],” it was not dealing with chalifin, which applies equally to a gentile and to an Israelite, but rather with a distinct mode of acquisition, such as money or pulling.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:6:1.hebrew: מצות חליצה קודמת - מה שפי' רבינו חננאל, פי' פרק החולץ (יבמות דף לט:):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:6:1.english: "The mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence" - What Rabbeinu Chananel explained [regarding this], he explained in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 39b).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:7:1.hebrew: מצות גאולה קודמת באדון שנאמר ואם לא יגאל - בערכין פרק המקדיש שדהו (ערכין דף כז.) מפ' טעם אחר דבעלים קודמין: לפי שמוסיפין חומש; והתם פריך לה ומשני:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 13a:7:1.english: "The mitzvah of redemption takes precedence for the owner, as it is stated: 'And if it is not redeemed'" - In Arakhin, in the chapter [entitled] HaMakdish Sedehu (Arakhin 27a), [the Mishnah] explains another reason that the owner takes precedence: because he adds a fifth; and there [the Gemara] challenges this and resolves [it].
